1.text: [The time of] their account has approached for the people, while they are in heedlessness turning away.

2.text: No mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are at play

3.text: With their hearts distracted. And those who do wrong conceal their private conversation, [saying], "Is this [Prophet] except a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you are aware [of it]?"

4.text: He [the Prophet (ﷺ)] said, "My Lord knows whatever is said throughout the heaven and earth, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing."

5.text: But they say, "[The revelation is but] a mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the previous [messengers] were sent [with miracles]."

6.text: Not a [single] city which We destroyed believed before them,<sup foot_note="227253">1</sup> so will they believe?

footnotes.227253: - Even though they had witnessed signs and miracles.

7.text: And We sent not before you, [O Muḥammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message [i.e., former scriptures] if you do not know.

8.text: And We did not make them [i.e., the prophets] forms not eating food,<sup foot_note="227254">1</sup> nor were they immortal [on earth].

footnotes.227254: - Like the angels.  Rather, they were human beings with human attributes.

9.text: Then<sup foot_note="227255">1</sup> We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors.

footnotes.227255: - Once they had conveyed the message.

10.text: We have certainly sent down to you a Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] in which is your mention.<sup foot_note="227256">1</sup> Then will you not reason?

footnotes.227256: - This implies the honor of having been mentioned or addressed.  Another meaning is "your reminder."

11.text: And how many a city which was unjust<sup foot_note="227257">1</sup> have We shattered and produced after it another people.

footnotes.227257: - i.e., its inhabitants persisting in wrongdoing.

12.text: And when they [i.e., its inhabitants] perceived Our punishment, at once they fled from it.

13.text: [Some angels said], "Do not flee but return to where you were given luxury and to your homes - perhaps you will be questioned."<sup foot_note="227258">1</sup>

footnotes.227258: - About what happened to you.  This is said to them in sarcasm and ridicule.

14.text: They said, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."

15.text: And that declaration of theirs did not cease until We made them [as] a harvest [mowed down], extinguished [like a fire].

16.text: And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them in play.

17.text: Had We intended to take a diversion,<sup foot_note="227259">1</sup> We could have taken it from [what is] with Us - if [indeed] We were to do so.

footnotes.227259: - Such as a wife or a child.

18.text: Rather, We dash the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it,<sup foot_note="227260">1</sup> and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from that which you describe.<sup foot_note="227261">2</sup>

footnotes.227260: Literally, "strikes its brain," disabling or killing it.
footnotes.227261: Of untruth concerning Allāh, particularly here, the claim that He has a son or other "partner" in divinity.

19.text: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him [i.e., the angels] are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.

20.text: They exalt [Him] night and day [and] do not slacken.

21.text: Or have they [i.e., men] taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?

22.text: Had there been within them [i.e., the heavens and earth] gods besides Allāh, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allāh, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.

23.text: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.

24.text: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, [O Muḥammad], "Produce your proof. This [Qur’ān] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me."<sup foot_note="227262">1</sup> But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.

footnotes.227262: - All previous prophets called for the worship of Allāh alone.

25.text: And We sent not before you any messenger except We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."

26.text: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they<sup foot_note="227263">1</sup> are [but] honored servants.

footnotes.227263: - Those they claim to be "children" of Allāh, such as the angels, Ezra, Jesus, etc.

27.text: They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command.

28.text: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them,<sup foot_note="227264">1</sup> and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.

29.text: And whoever of them should say, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him" - that one We would recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.

30.text: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and then We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?

31.text: And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein [mountain] passes [as] roads that they might be guided.

32.text: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs,<sup foot_note="227265">1</sup> are turning away.

footnotes.227265: - The signs present in the heavens.

33.text: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.

34.text: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal?

35.text: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial; and to Us you will be returned.

36.text: And when those who disbelieve see you, [O Muḥammad], they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one who mentions [i.e., insults] your gods?" And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers.

37.text: Man was created of haste [i.e., impatience]. I will show you My signs [i.e., vengeance], so do not impatiently urge Me.

38.text: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"

39.text: If those who disbelieved but knew the time when they will not avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs and they will not be aided...<sup foot_note="227266">1</sup>

footnotes.227266: - The completion of the sentence is understood to be "...they would not be asking in disbelief and ridicule to be shown the punishment."

40.text: Rather, it will come to them unexpectedly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved.

41.text: And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.

42.text: Say, "Who can protect you at night or by day from the Most Merciful?" But they are, from the remembrance of their Lord, turning away.

43.text: Or do they have gods to defend them other than Us? They are unable [even] to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.

44.text: But, [on the contrary], We have provided good things for these [disbelievers] and their fathers until life was prolonged for them. Then do they not see that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders?<sup foot_note="227267">1</sup> Is it they who will overcome?

45.text: Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.

46.text: And if [as much as] a whiff of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers."

47.text: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed,<sup foot_note="227268">1</sup> We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.

footnotes.227268: - i.e., anything as small or insignificant as a mustard seed.

48.text: And We had already given Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder<sup foot_note="227269">1</sup> for the righteous

footnotes.227269: - These are three qualities of the Torah.

49.text: Who fear their Lord unseen,<sup foot_note="227270">1</sup> while they are of the Hour apprehensive.

footnotes.227270: - Which can mean "Him being unseen" by them or "though they are unseen" by others.

50.text: And this [Qur’ān] is a blessed message which We have sent down. Then are you with it unacquainted?<sup foot_note="227271">1</sup>

footnotes.227271: - i.e., pretending ignorance, disapproving or refusing to acknowledge it?

51.text: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before,<sup foot_note="227272">1</sup> and We were of him well-Knowing

footnotes.227272: - i.e., before Moses.  Allāh had guided him from early youth.

52.text: When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"

53.text: They said, "We found our fathers worshippers of them."

54.text: He said, "You were certainly, you and your fathers, in manifest error."

55.text: They said, "Have you come to us with truth, or are you of those who jest?"

56.text: He said, "[No], rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I, to that, am of those who testify.

57.text: And [I swear] by Allāh, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away."

58.text: So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question].

59.text: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers."

60.text: They said, "We heard a young man mention them who is called Abraham."

61.text: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."<sup foot_note="227273">1</sup>

footnotes.227273: - To what they had heard him say.  It may also mean "...that they may witness [what will be done to him as punishment]."

62.text: They said, "Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham?"

63.text: He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak."

64.text: So they returned to [blaming] themselves and said [to each other], "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."

65.text: Then they reversed themselves,<sup foot_note="227274">1</sup> [saying], "You have already known that these do not speak!"

footnotes.227274: - After first admitting their error, they were seized by pride and obstinacy.

66.text: He said, "Then do you worship instead of Allāh that which does not benefit you at all or harm you?

67.text: Uff<sup foot_note="227275">1</sup> to you and to what you worship instead of Allāh. Then will you not use reason?"

footnotes.227275: - An exclamation of anger and displeasure.

68.text: They said, "Burn him and support your gods - if you are to act."

69.text: We [i.e., Allāh] said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."

70.text: And they intended for him a plan [i.e., harm], but We made them the greatest losers.

71.text: And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds [i.e., peoples].

72.text: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob in addition, and all [of them] We made righteous.

73.text: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakāh; and they were worshippers of Us.

74.text: And to Lot We gave judgement and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that was committing wicked deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.

75.text: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous.

76.text: And [mention] Noah, when he called [to Allāh]<sup foot_note="227276">1</sup> before [that time], so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great affliction [i.e., the flood].

footnotes.227276: - i.e., supplicated against his people who had persisted in denial and animosity.  See 71:26-28.

77.text: And We aided [i.e., saved] him from the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them, all together.

78.text: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of a people overran it [at night],<sup foot_note="227277">1</sup> and We were witness to their judgement.

79.text: And We gave understanding of it [i.e., the case] to Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to exalt [Us], along with David and [also] the birds. And We were doing [that].<sup foot_note="227278">1</sup>

footnotes.227278: - Meaning that Allāh has always been capable of accomplishing whatever He wills.

80.text: And We taught him the fashioning of coats of armor to protect you from your [enemy in] battle. So will you then be grateful?

81.text: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, proceeding by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing.

82.text: And of the devils [i.e., jinn] were those who dived for him and did work other than that. And We were of them a guardian.<sup foot_note="227279">1</sup>

footnotes.227279: - Preventing any disobedience or deviation by them from Solomon's instructions and protecting him from being harmed by them.

83.text: And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."

84.text: So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of Allāh].

85.text: And [mention] Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient.

86.text: And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.

87.text: And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger<sup foot_note="227280">1</sup> and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him.<sup foot_note="227281">2</sup> And he called out within the darknesses,<sup foot_note="227282">3</sup> "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."

footnotes.227280: At the disbelief of his people.
footnotes.227281: Or "would not restrict him" in the belly of the fish.
footnotes.227282: That of the night, of the sea, and of the fish's interior.

88.text: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.

89.text: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors."

90.text: So We responded to him, and We gave to him John, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate<sup foot_note="227283">1</sup> Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.

91.text: And [mention] the one who guarded her chastity [i.e., Mary], so We blew into her [garment] through Our angel [i.e., Gabriel], and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.

92.text: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion,<sup foot_note="227284">1</sup> and I am your Lord, so worship Me.

footnotes.227284: - i.e., a collective way of life or course of conduct followed by a community.

93.text: And [yet] they divided their affair [i.e., that of their religion] among themselves,<sup foot_note="227285">1</sup> [but] all to Us will return.

94.text: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - no denial will there be for his effort,<sup foot_note="227286">1</sup> and indeed We [i.e., Our angels], of it, are recorders.

footnotes.227286: - Such a person will not be deprived of his due reward.

95.text: And it is prohibited to [the people of] a city which We have destroyed that they will [ever] return<sup foot_note="227287">1</sup>

footnotes.227287: - They cannot return to this world, nor can they repent to Allāh.

96.text: Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend

97.text: And [when] the true promise [i.e., the resurrection] has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring [in horror, while they say], "O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."

98.text: Indeed, you [disbelievers] and what you worship other than Allāh are the firewood of Hell. You will be coming to [enter] it.

99.text: Had these [false deities] been [actual] gods, they would not have come to it, but all are eternal therein.

100.text: For them therein is heavy sighing, and they therein will not hear.

101.text: Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us - they are from it far removed.

102.text: They will not hear its sound, while they are, in that which their souls desire, abiding eternally.

103.text: They will not be grieved by the greatest terror,<sup foot_note="227288">1</sup> and the angels will meet them, [saying], "This is your Day which you have been promised" -

footnotes.227288: - The events of the Last Hour or of the Resurrection.

104.text: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.<sup foot_note="227289">1</sup>

footnotes.227289: - More literally, "Indeed, We are ever doers" of what We will.

105.text: And We have already written in the book [of Psalms]<sup foot_note="227290">1</sup> after the [previous] mention<sup foot_note="227291">2</sup> that the land [of Paradise] is inherited by My righteous servants.

footnotes.227290: Az-Zabūr can also mean "scriptures" in general.
footnotes.227291: i.e., the Torah.  The "mention" may also refer to the original inscription with Allāh, i.e., the Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

106.text: Indeed, in this [Qur’ān] is notification for a worshipping people.

107.text: And We have not sent you, [O Muḥammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.

108.text: Say, "It is only revealed to me that your god is but one God; so will you be Muslims [in submission to Him]?"

109.text: But if they turn away, then say, "I have announced to [all of] you equally.<sup foot_note="227292">1</sup> And I know not whether near or far is that which you are promised.

footnotes.227292: - The Prophet (ﷺ) made this message known to all people, not concealing any of it from anyone or preferring any group over another.

110.text: Indeed, He knows what is declared of speech, and He knows what you conceal.

111.text: And I know not; perhaps it<sup foot_note="227293">1</sup> is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time."

112.text: [The Prophet (ﷺ)] has said, "My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one whose help is sought against that which you describe."<sup foot_note="227294">1</sup>
